title: Surjectivity of a representable morphism can be tested on finite presentation affines
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism over $S$-schemes of categories fibred in groupoids (categories with cartesian lifts along every base map and groupoid fibres). Suppose $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space]: for each $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal G(T)$, the $2$-fibre product $\mathcal F\times_{\mathcal G}h_T$, whose objects are triples $(a,t,\alpha:f(a)\cong y|_t)$, is an algebraic space $W_y$ over $T$. Here $h_T$ is the groupoid of maps into $T$, with only identity arrows. Assume $\mathcal G$ is limit preserving on objects: for every small directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes $T_i$ with limit $T$, every object of $\mathcal G(T)$ is isomorphic to the pullback of an object of some $\mathcal G(T_i)$. If $W_y\to T$ is surjective for every affine $S$-scheme $T$ locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and every $y\in\mathcal G(T)$, then $W_y\to T$ is surjective for every $S$-scheme $T$ and every $y\in\mathcal G(T)$. Surjectivity here means surjectivity on points, where points of an algebraic space are field-valued maps modulo common field extensions [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

proof.text: First record the formal base-change identification used below. For an $S$-map $u:T'\to T$, an object $y\in\mathcal G(T)$ and an isomorphism $\sigma:u^*y\cong y'$, one has $W_{y'}\cong W_y\times_TT'$ over $T'$; the right side exists by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Indeed, on a test $v:Z\to T'$, compose an isomorphism $\alpha:f(a)\cong v^*y'$ with $(v^*\sigma)^{-1}$ to obtain $f(a)\cong(uv)^*y$. Composition with $v^*\sigma$ reverses this operation, on both objects and arrows. These operations commute with pullback (using the cartesian-lift identifications), so they identify the two represented functors on test schemes. Morphisms of algebraic spaces are natural transformations by [def-trf-algebraic-space], so the inverse transformations give the asserted isomorphism, with the projection to $T'$ unchanged.

source.place: Tag 07WI (lemma-check-property-limit-preserving), last sentence: the identity F_y = F_{y_i} times_{V_i} V; formal identification expanded on test objects

proof.text: For now let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be affine, with structure map factoring through an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$, so that $A$ is an $R$-algebra. Following the second proof of Stacks 00QN, let $I$ be the set of pairs $(E,K)$ with $E\subseteq A$ finite and $K\subseteq R[X_e;e\in E]$ a finite set of polynomials vanishing under $X_e\mapsto e$, ordered by $(E,K)\le(E',K')$ iff $E\subseteq E'$ and $K\subseteq K'$ inside $R[X_e;e\in E']$. It is a subset of a set built from $A$, hence small; $(\emptyset,\emptyset)\in I$, and $(E\cup E',K\cup K')$ bounds two pairs, so $I$ is a nonempty directed set. Put $A_{(E,K)}=R[X_e;e\in E]/(K)$, finitely presented over $R$, with the $R$-algebra maps $X_e\mapsto e$ to $A$ and $X_e\mapsto X_e$ between the stages; they are compatible. Write $i=(E,K)$ and $A_i=A_{(E,K)}$ below. This is a colimit in $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Given compatible $R$-algebra maps $b_{(E,K)}:A_{(E,K)}\to B$, put $\phi(a)=b_{(\{a\},\emptyset)}(X_a)$; compatibility gives $b_{(E,K)}(X_e)=\phi(e)$ for all $e\in E$. The stages $(\{a,a',a+a',aa'\},\{X_{a+a'}-X_a-X_{a'},X_{aa'}-X_aX_{a'}\})$, $(\{1\},\{X_1-1\})$ and $(\{a,ra\},\{X_{ra}-rX_a\})$ show that $\phi$ is an $R$-algebra map, and then $\phi$ composed with $A_{(E,K)}\to A$ agrees with $b_{(E,K)}$ on the generators $X_e$. Any compatible $u:A\to B$ has $u(a)=b_{(\{a\},\emptyset)}(X_a)=\phi(a)$, which gives uniqueness. The index set is chosen explicitly because the hypothesis on $\mathcal G$ is stated for small directed systems.

source.place: Tag 00QN (lemma-ring-colimit-fp), second proof: the directed set of pairs (S, E) and the algebras A_{S,E}; the colimit check that Stacks calls clear is written out

proof.text: The same cocone is a colimit in commutative rings. To check its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], take any compatible ring maps $b_i:A_i\to B$. Their composites $R\to B$ agree, since any two indices have a common upper bound and all transition maps are $R$-linear; nonemptiness supplies one such composite. Equip $B$ with this $R$-algebra structure. The $R$-algebra colimit property from step 2 gives a unique compatible map $A\to B$. Conversely any compatible ring map $A\to B$ must induce this same map on $R$, by factoring $R\to A$ through any $A_i$, so uniqueness also holds among ring maps.

source.place: Tag 00QN (lemma-ring-colimit-fp), its directed algebra-colimit presentation viewed as a ring colimit; universal-property verification

proof.text: Put $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit], the scheme $V$ with its actual projections is the inverse limit of the affine schemes $V_i$. All maps are over $U$, hence over $S$, because the ring maps are $R$-algebra maps. The scheme-limit universal property also holds over $S$: any factorization through $V$ respects its $S$-structure after composing with any one projection, and the directed index set is nonempty. Each $V_i\to S$ is locally of finite presentation by [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]: at every point use the whole affine source $V_i$, the affine open $U$ of the original target $S$, and the finitely presented ring map $R\to A_i$. In particular no quasi-separatedness or quasi-compactness assumption on $S$ is being used.

source.place: Tag 07WI (lemma-check-property-limit-preserving), affine inverse-limit presentation; Limits Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit); finite-presentation chart from Morphisms Tag 01TP (definition-finite-presentation)

proof.text: Let $y\in\mathcal G(V)$. The limit-preserving-on-objects hypothesis now gives an index $i$, an object $y_i\in\mathcal G(V_i)$ and an isomorphism $p_i^*y_i\cong y$. The representability hypothesis gives the algebraic space $W_{y_i}$ over $V_i$. Since $V_i$ is affine and locally of finite presentation over $S$, the test hypothesis says precisely that $W_{y_i}\to V_i$ is surjective on point classes. Step 1 identifies $W_y\to V$ with the base change of this morphism along $p_i:V\to V_i$. Only descent of this single object is needed: no full faithfulness on arrows and no limit preservation of $\mathcal F$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 07WI (lemma-check-property-limit-preserving), proof: y comes from y_i by (2), and F_{y_i} to V_i has the property by (3)

proof.text: Prove this base change is surjective directly with the point convention of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Represent a point of $V$ by $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$. Surjectivity of $W_{y_i}\to V_i$ gives a representative $b:\operatorname{Spec}L\to W_{y_i}$ whose image point is the point of $p_i a$. Equality of these point classes means that after maps from $K$ and $L$ into a common extension field $M$, the two maps to $V_i$ agree. Thus $(b|_M,a|_M)$ is an $M$-valued point of $W_{y_i}\times_{V_i}V$, and its projection represents the original point of $V$. Step 1 gives the required point of $W_y$. This proves the assertion whenever $V$ is affine and maps into an affine open of $S$; if $V$ has no points the same surjectivity assertion is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 03H4 (lemma-points-cartesian), common-field-extension proof; Tag 03BU (definition-points). This expands base-change stability used at the end of Tag 07WI

proof.text: Finally take an arbitrary $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal G(T)$. Represent any point class of $T$ by $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$, with image $t$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] first on $S$ to choose an affine open $U$ containing the image of $t$, and then on $T$ to choose an affine open $V$ with $t\in V\subseteq T\times_SU$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has one point, its map factors through $V$ by the open-subscheme description in [def-weil-open-immersion]. Steps 2-6 applied to $y|_V$ give a point of $W_{y|_V}$ above the resulting point of $V$. Step 1 identifies this space with $W_y\times_TV$; its projection to $W_y$ therefore gives a point above the original point of $T$. Every point has been lifted, proving surjectivity. This includes the empty $T$, for which there is no point to lift, and does not require affine intersections or a finite covering.
